::: {.callout-important}
**Series Context** — Volume VI Book 01. This is the deployable realization of **Volume I (Foundation & Transport)**: the landing zone, IPAM/DDI naming-and-addressing plane, and the SASE/TIC distributed policy-enforcement edge, expressed as infrastructure-as-code applied through the Book VI-00 pipeline.
:::

# What This Document Addresses

Volume I argues that authoritative naming/addressing and a distributed enforcement edge are the only mechanisms that close the DNS-authority, boundary-protection, and component-inventory controls. This book carries the code that stands them up: the landing-zone scaffolding, the DDI plane, and the enforcement-edge configuration, so the closure Volume I designs is reproducible from source rather than assembled by hand.

# Deployable Artifacts

| Artifact | Realizes (Vol I) | Deployed example | Multi-CSP substitution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Landing-zone module (management groups, subscriptions, policy assignment) | Governed cloud foundation | Azure Landing Zone (Bicep/Terraform) | AWS Control Tower + Terraform; GCP org policy |
| Network module (hub-spoke, segmentation, NGFW/route intent) | SC-7 boundary + traffic-class separation | Terraform (VNet, Azure Firewall) | AWS VPC + Network Firewall; GCP VPC-SC |
| DDI module (authoritative DNS, DNSSEC signing, RPZ, DHCP scopes) | SC-20/21/22 naming plane; CM-8 address-keyed inventory | InfoBlox / cloud DNS as code | BlueCat; Route 53 + IPAM |
| Enforcement-edge config (SASE/TIC 3.0 PEP capability set) | AC-4 flow enforcement at the distributed PEP | SASE tenant-as-code | Zscaler/Netskope GovCloud config-as-code |

# Closure Necessity

::: {.callout-tip}
## Closure Necessity — a source of truth you cannot re-derive is not one
Volume I's claim is that no scanner *creates* authoritative naming or inventory — it only measures drift from a source of truth. This book is what makes that source of truth **reproducible**: an IPAM/DDI plane and a boundary defined in code can be re-derived, diffed, and attested. A hand-built landing zone cannot satisfy CM-8's "authoritative inventory" claim because there is no authority to point at.
:::

# Controls Operationalized

| Control | Title | How this book deploys it |
|---|---|---|
| SC-7 | Boundary Protection | Segmentation + NGFW/route intent as code at the enforcement edge |
| SC-20/21/22 | Secure Name/Address Resolution | DNSSEC-signing authoritative + validating recursive resolvers as code; RPZ |
| CM-8 | System Component Inventory | Address-keyed inventory derived from the IPAM source of truth |
| AC-4 | Information Flow Enforcement | Application-aware flow policy at the SASE/TIC PEP |
